invariant-native-syscall-dispatch: NativeSyscallRegistry (native/angr/src/syscalls/mod.rs; the SyscallOutcome/SyscallError/NativeSyscall vocabulary it dispatches through lives in the sibling syscalls/support.rs and is re-exported, so crate::syscalls::X paths are unchanged) mirrors NativeProcedureRegistry: HashMap keyed by (arch_name, syscall_num). Wired into exploration/stepping.rs at the RunResult::Syscall arm — try native dispatch before creating PendingCallback. Three outcomes: SyscallOutcome::Continue{ret} writes ret to return_register; SyscallOutcome::ContinueSymbolic{ret} writes the BV directly with set_register_by_offset (no concrete wrap); SyscallOutcome::Exit pushes to STASH_DEADENDED. All honor deferred_forks via process_deferred_forks_into. Handler returning Err falls back to the Python callback path (see invariant-syscall-fallback-on-collision for the brk-style 'pre-empt before mutate' pattern). SyscallOutcome derives Debug (needed for #[test] expect_err). Registry covers AMD64/X86/ARM/ARM64/MIPS32/MIPS64/CGC tables — register_syscalls! macro declared in mod.rs just above NativeSyscallRegistry::new. See the seven register_syscalls! invocations inside NativeSyscallRegistry::new (AMD64/X86/ARM/ARM64/MIPS32/MIPS64/CGC, each under its own banner comment) for live lists; do NOT enumerate them in memory (drifts within weeks).
invariant-native-syscall-linux-divergenc: Native-syscall vs Python-procedure divergence policy (rust-symex). Native handlers in native/angr/src/syscalls/ normally MIRROR the angr Python procedure, but there is a standing exception: when the Python procedure's behavior on a degenerate input is *silently wrong* (accepts a request it cannot honor and reports success), the native handler may instead implement real-Linux semantics and return the kernel's errno-style failure. Established by angr-ttr7 (MAP_FIXED collision: Python returns -1, native unmaps+remaps like Linux) and extended by angr-sqfj8.110 (misaligned MAP_FIXED addr: Python silently floors it to the containing page via page-granular map_region, native returns -1 = EINVAL as Linux do_mmap's offset_in_page(addr) check does). **How to apply:** justified only when (a) real Linux has an unambiguous answer, (b) Python's answer is silently-wrong rather than merely different, and (c) real toolchains never emit the input, so exploration parity is not actually at risk. Record the divergence in the handler's module doc next to the existing policy list — do NOT leave it implicit, since a future reader diffing against the Python proc will otherwise read it as a bug. Distinguish carefully from a *hint*-shaped arg (non-MAP_FIXED mmap addr), where round-down IS correct and must stay Python-identical.
invariant-native-whitespace-single-sourc: invariant-ctype-mirror-python-not-rust-std sibling risk is now RETIRED: strtod.rs (floating_prefix_len + the endptr rescan in run_strtod) and strtol.rs (parse_concrete_prefix) no longer use Rust is_ascii_whitespace. All byte-level whitespace classification in native/angr/src/procedures/ goes through the single pub(crate) helper procedures::ctype::is_c_space (' ' plus 0x09..=0x0d) — grep for is_ascii_whitespace to verify no new site regresses. Since angr-6cp06.1 the table itself is the pub(crate) const procedures::ctype::C_SPACE_RANGES: is_c_space delegates to it and NativeIsSpace consumes it directly (NativeIsSpace can no longer call is_c_space, which takes a u8, because the proc must compare the full arch-word argument), so the two still cannot drift. SEMANTICS DECISION (angr-2j9sk, commit 2ce6e098c): native strtol/strtod match libc, NOT Python. angr/procedures/libc/strtol.py skips no leading whitespace at all and says so in a source comment ('note: this does not handle skipping white space'), i.e. an acknowledged gap rather than a modelled behaviour — so 'mirror Python' does not apply where Python has no behaviour to mirror. The mirror-Python rule governs ctype PREDICATES, where Python encodes a deliberate predicate.
invariant-nativesimprocedure-name-static: NativeSimProcedure::name() returns &'static str. For a procedure whose name is only known at runtime (Python-registered hooks, ReturnUnconstrained stubs), leak the String in the *constructor* and store the resulting &'static str in the field -- do NOT keep a String field and Box::leak inside name(), which leaks a fresh allocation on every call. Canonical sites: procedures/python_proc.rs::PythonNativeProcedure::new and procedures/stub.rs::NativeReturnUnconstrained::new. The leak is bounded (one allocation per registered procedure, process lifetime) and the registry holds an Arc<Self> anyway. For names that repeat (unmapped VEX opcodes), intern instead -- vex/opcode_map.rs::intern_unmapped_op. angr-91vj9.10.
invariant-next-id-global-not-adjacent: SymContext::next_id (native/angr/src/symbolic/bv_id_ops.rs) allocates from the PROCESS-GLOBAL NEXT_SYMBOL_ID atomic, not a per-context counter. Any Rust unit test asserting that two consecutive next_id() draws are ADJACENT (b == a + 1) is flaky under cargo test parallelism -- another test can take the id in between. This sank the iter203 ralph gate via symbolic::context::context_tests_lineage::test_fork (left 9732, right 9731). Assert strict monotonicity (b > a) instead; fork's real contract is 'keeps drawing from the same global sequence', not 'next id is exactly parent+1'. Fixed in angr-lzywj.
invariant-no-op-test-needs-inverted-cont: invariant: a test whose whole assertion is 'nothing happened' (a defensive/no-op branch, an ignored ping, a guard that returns early) must be proven non-vacuous before commit — temporarily invert the input so the branch is NOT taken and confirm the test fails, then restore. Same reasoning as the valgrind/rounding-mode gates' --self-test (CLAUDE.md): an assertion that has never been seen to fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot. Worked example: exploration/scheduler_tests.rs::test_wake_worker_out_of_range_id_is_noop asserts PersistentPool::wake_worker with worker_id past job_txs' end emits no upstream WorkerUp within 250ms; swapping the out-of-range ids for 0 must (and does) fail the recv_timeout assert, because a woken worker re-parks and emits a second Quiesced. Without that step the timeout would also 'pass' if the pool were simply dead.
invariant-no-registration-without-arch-g: Registering a native syscall handler on an arch its own `call` arch-guard rejects is a NO-OP WITH A COST, not a harmless placeholder: the dispatcher runs the native lookup, the guard returns SyscallError::Other, and the state falls back to Python anyway — one extra hop per call, forever. The correct expression of 'this arch isn't supported yet' is to NOT register the number in NativeSyscallRegistry::new (native/angr/src/syscalls/mod.rs). Precedent: MIPS64 stat (5004) / fstat (5005) were correctly unregistered while lstat (5006) / newfstatat (5252) were registered-then-rejected until angr-9ke6b.154 removed them. The governing oracle for the stat family is the STAT_LAYOUT_WRITERS table in syscalls/file_path/stat_layouts.rs (see invariant-stat-family-arch-coverage) — an arch absent from that table must not appear in any stat-family registration. Since angr-6cp06.53 the handlers' guards derive from that table via require_stat_arch, so adding a new arch means adding the writer table entry AND the registration together (there is no longer a separate guard arm to forget). Cross-check tool: for each arch, `awk -v a='"ARCH",' 'index($0,a){f=1} f&&/^        \);/{f=0} f' mod.rs | grep Native<X>Syscall` vs the STAT_LAYOUT_WRITERS entries.
invariant-no-zero-fill-symbolic-store: Symbolic-store zero-fill is a hard error, not a fallback (angr-9ke6b.19, commit 69c0ef344). bv_to_bytes (both copies: interpreter/bv_utils.rs and callbacks/dispatch.rs) returns all-ZERO bytes for a symbolic RustBV, so any 'fall back to the byte-level memory_store callback' path is sound ONLY for concrete values. Four sites used to take it unconditionally when memory_store_symbolic_value was unwired, reporting success while overwriting memory with 0: call_memory_store_symbolic_value's own fallback, statements.rs::handle_storeg (concrete-addr AND concretized-Single arms of the symbolic-guard StoreG path), statements_cas.rs::cas_store_symbolic_data (concrete addr), statements_store.rs::handle_symbolic_store (Single arm). Now all four reject a symbolic value: interpreter/bv_utils.rs::reject_symbolic_byte_store(value, addr, site) -> CbExecutionError::Unsupported is the single rule for the three interpreter sites, and call_memory_store_symbolic_value raises PyRuntimeError on its own path. Concrete values still take the byte fallback unchanged. Rule for new store paths: never hand a possibly-symbolic RustBV to bv_to_bytes + call_memory_store — either route through call_memory_store_symbolic_value / _symbolic_full, or call reject_symbolic_byte_store first. Latent in production (rust_manager.py::_setup_callbacks always registers the callback), live for minimal embeddings and bare PythonCallbacks::new() test harnesses. Sibling invariant on the buffering side: invariant-symbolic-store-no-zero-bytes. Pinned by dispatch_tests.rs::store_symbolic_value_without_callback_errors_instead_of_zero_filling and statements_tests.rs::cas_symbolic_store_without_callback_errors_not_zero_fills. UPDATE (angr-sqfj8.61, commit 3456b308a): the same wrong answer has a SECOND shape — CONCRETIZE-then-store fallbacks. statements_store.rs::handle_concrete_store, when memory_store_symbolic_value errored, did ctx.eval(&data_val).unwrap_or(0) and wrote that; an unsat/unknown context or a >128-bit value therefore zero-filled while returning Ok(()). Rule extension: an eval-based concretization fallback must NEVER unwrap_or(0) — propagate the original error (Option -> loud Err + log::warn!). Also use symbolic::u128_to_le_bytes with a MAX_CONCRETE_CHUNK (16-byte) guard rather than a hand-rolled `(v >> (i*8)) as u8` loop, which silently wraps mod 128 past 16 bytes. Pinned by statements_tests.rs::symbolic_store_fallback_errors_instead_of_zero_filling_when_eval_fails (+ the _writes_concretized_bytes_when_eval_succeeds converse).

invariant-opcode-map-ground-truth-is-ven: Before adding or trusting an IROp arm in native/angr/src/vex/opcode_map.rs or its opcode_map_float.rs / opcode_map_vector.rs siblings (angr-fs8kb.20 moved parse_float/parse_transcendental and parse_vector/parse_vreverse/parse_neon_unimplemented out of the parent), grep native/angr/vendor/pyvex_ffi.h for the exact Iop_ string — it is the vendored libVEX opcode enum and therefore the ground truth for what a real lift can emit. Two whole families were dead code that read as implemented coverage until angr-9ke6b.161/.162 (commit bad76646f): scalar Iop_MulHi{32,64}{S,U} (only vector Iop_MulHi<w>{U,S}x<n> exist; x86 IMUL/MUL lift to Iop_MullS32/Iop_MullU32 + Iop_64HIto32) and scalar Iop_Neg{8,16,32,64} (only float Iop_NegF32/Iop_NegF64 -> IROp::FNeg, the unmappable Iop_NegF128 -- IRType has no F128 variant -- and vector Iop_Neg32Fx2/Iop_Neg32Fx4/Iop_Neg64Fx2 exist; there is NO Iop_NegF16, so do not re-copy the old Iop_Neg{F16,F32,F64,F128} brace-enumeration this memory used to carry, corrected in angr-fs8kb.19; integer negation lifts as 0-x via Iop_Sub). The tell for this class: an opcode_map arm whose IROp variant has zero references in any *_tests*.rs — parse_opcode falls through to IROp::Unmapped for a name nobody emits, so the arm never fires and no test ever notices. The QDMulHi/QRDMulHi high-half vector family is genuinely unmapped (see invariant-qdmull-vex-op), which is a different thing from unreachable. The mirror-image shape also exists and is INTENTIONAL: an IROp variant that is fully implemented and tested but has no opcode_map producer because libVEX has no such opcode. IROp::ModS/ModU (no Iop_Mod* exists; guests use the combined Iop_DivMod*, and VEXOps::divmod_double_to_single takes its remainder straight from RustBV::urem/srem) and the bare 1-bit IROp::FCmp{EQ,LT,LE} (every real float compare carries a width/lane suffix -> FCmpScalarLane/FCmpVecPacked; suffix-free Iop_CmpF32/64 is the three-way FComCC and suffix-free Iop_CmpEQ8/16/32/64 are integer) are both documented as such at their ops_def.rs definition sites since angr-fs8kb.17/.18 — do not re-file them as dispatch gaps, and document any new one the same way.
invariant-option-gated-symbolic-addr-tes: Testing an option-gated symbolic-address branch (AVOID_MULTIVALUED_READS/WRITES, and any future gate spelled `option && addr.as_u64().is_none()`): build the address as a BVS pinned by a solver constraint to ONE concrete location. `as_u64()` stays None so the gate fires, yet the concretizer resolves to exactly one address when it does not — so the ON and OFF runs differ ONLY by the short-circuit, with no multi-solution ITE noise to explain away. Canonical harness: `memory/tests/avoid_multivalued.rs::pinned_symbolic_addr` (mirrored as `mv_write_addr` in `interpreter/statements_tests.rs` and `pinned_symbolic_addr` in `interpreter/expressions_tests.rs`). Corollary from angr-6cp06.67: per-site sabotage is the only way to learn a gate is REDUNDANT — `VEXInterpreter::try_rust_memory_load`'s copy of the read short-circuit is unobservable on its own because `SymbolicMemory::load_symbolic_unified` carries the same gate downstream. Say so in the test's doc comment instead of writing an assertion that pretends otherwise.
invariant-overflow-fix-refuse-not-satura: Overflow fix choice: saturating_add is right for SIZES/LENGTHS but WRONG for IDENTITIES (fd numbers, allocation slots, ids) — clamping hands the same identity out twice and aliases two live objects, which is a worse wrong answer than the plain + it replaced. For identity allocators, use checked_add and REFUSE (return None/Err so the caller bounces to Python), mirroring FileSystem::dup2's MAX_FD refusal. Applied in FileSystem::pipe (angr-03vl4.55): saturating would have returned u32::MAX for BOTH pipe ends. Contrast round_alloc_size (state/process.rs) where saturating IS correct — the value is a size, so clamping only over-reserves. Related: mixed-signedness position arithmetic wants neither — FileSystem::seek's offset_position widens u64 base + i64 offset to i128 and clamps, because 'base as i64 + offset' is wrong twice (i64 overflow AND a base above i64::MAX going negative before the offset applies). ESCAPE HATCH (angr-0jh0j.50, state/process.rs::advance_brk): an identity allocator whose -> u64 contract has no failure channel may saturate instead of refusing, but only when (a) wrapping would alias *mapped* memory while saturating aliases only the unreachable top of the address space, and (b) the saturation is logged (silent_default!(cat_c, ...)). Do not read that as license to saturate an identity that has a callable refusal path.
invariant-overflow-guard-test-operand-sh: Overflow-guard regression tests must pick operands whose WRAPPING product/sum is benign, not merely huge — otherwise the test passes under both spellings and pins nothing. For a saturating_mul size*count guard, u64::MAX*2 is the wrong choice (wraps to u64::MAX-1, still over the cap, so the oversize branch fires either way); 2^63*2 is right (wraps to exactly 0, which takes the zero-total early-return and reports a successful no-op for a 2^64-byte request). Canonical pair: procedures/fwrite_tests.rs::test_fwrite_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping and procedures/fread_tests.rs::test_fread_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping (angr-0jh0j.40/.43). Always mutation-check: swap saturating_mul -> wrapping_mul, confirm the new test FAILS, revert. Release builds set no overflow-checks so the wrapping result is what ships; a checked-profile panic is a second, weaker net.
invariant-page-bitmap-authoritative:
Page bitmap is the AUTHORITATIVE source of truth for byte-level symbolic-vs-concrete state in SymbolicMemory, NOT symbolic_objects/symbolic_spans. The sidecar maps (symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects) are caches/indexes that can lag behind page-bitmap-driven state. store_concrete's page.store_concrete correctly clears the bitmap bits but does NOT clean wider-sym sidecar entries based at a different address. Any load fast path that returns a sym (or extract) without first verifying the bitmap is buggy. See bytes_all_marked_symbolic helper (memory/mod.rs angr-jvjf) for the bitmap consultation pattern.

COROLLARY for merge repair loops (angr-fs8kb.68). SymbolicMemory::merge's trailing adopt-from-other backfill iterates other.symbolic_objects keyed at each object's BASE address. Gating that repair on `Entry::Vacant` at the base key is wrong: OCCUPIED != RESOLVABLE. The both-present per-byte walk earlier in merge legitimately overwrites the base key with a fresh 8-BIT ITE, so for an object straddling a page boundary (base page both-present, tail page other-only) the Vacant test fails and the tail bytes' symbolic_spans inserts are skipped entirely — bitmap-symbolic with no sidecar resolving them, load errors out. Two generalizable rules: (1) the resolvability predicate is per byte, `SymbolicMemory::symbolic_byte_lane(...).is_some()`, never `map.contains_key(base)`; (2) you cannot repair by re-pointing symbolic_spans at the base — symbolic_byte_lane rejects a span whose recorded width disagrees with the base object's actual width — so install an 8-bit self-referential entry per byte, the same shape the both-present walk uses. Gate the repair on the bitmap (this memory) AND on the byte not being Multi (see [[invariant-multi-vs-symbolic-cell-states]]), or you manufacture the inconsistent fourth cell state. Behavioural coverage lives in memory/tests/merge_sidecars.rs; this is the third recurrence of the adopt-the-bitmap-forget-the-sidecar shape after angr-c7xno.50 (multi_objects) and angr-91vj9.3 (interior symbolic_spans).
invariant-page-move-carries-sidecars: INVARIANT (page-granular moves vs flat side tables): MemoryPage carries only data + symbolic_bitmap + multi_bitmap. The per-address payloads (SymbolicMemory::symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects, multi_versions) are FLAT maps on SymbolicMemory, not nested in the page — so any path that inserts/clones/adopts a whole page from another SymbolicMemory (merge's (None,Some(op)) arm, snapshot restore, migration, prefetch) must copy the matching side-table entries explicitly or it installs bitmap bits pointing at nothing. Orphaned Multi bits are especially bad: range_has_multi (load.rs) gates on multi_objects, NOT the bitmap, so the load silently returns the stale concrete byte, and merge's 's_multi implies a payload' expect panics on the next merge. Fixed for merge in angr-c7xno.50 by walking MemoryPage::multi_offsets (mirrors symbolic_offsets) and routing payloads through the existing multi_ops queue so set_multi_alternatives does the bitmap sync + bump_multi_version. Note this is the inverse direction of invariant-page-bitmap-authoritative: the bitmap is authoritative for READS, but it is not self-sufficient for MOVES.
invariant-panic-abort-not-under-cargo-te: panic=abort is NOT in effect under cargo test. The workspace sets panic="abort" only in [profile.release] (root Cargo.toml), and cargo FORCES panic="unwind" on test/bench harness binaries regardless of the profile's panic setting (libtest needs to unwind to report a failing test); no [profile.test] override can opt back into abort. Consequence for panic-hardening audits in native/angr/src/: any 'this .expect is provably unreachable because panic=abort forecloses mutex poisoning / thread death' argument holds for the SHIPPED .so only, never for 'cargo test --release --lib' (the ralph gate's first check). Concretely in exploration/scheduler.rs (Panic policy module header) + scheduler_worker.rs: under cargo test a worker that panics while holding the job.results / job.summaries guard (worker::worker_loop's terminal+summary drains, worker::drain_local_into_results) poisons that lock, and the coordinator's next lock -- WaveJob::take_results, WaveJob::into_results, or the done_rx guard in PersistentPool::run_wave -- fires its .expect("... poisoned") as a SECOND, cascaded panic. That cascade is expected, not a violated invariant: when debugging, ignore the 'mutex poisoned' panic and look for the EARLIEST panic in the test output. Scoped into the module doc by angr-9ke6b.57 (commit c9d2f3e5d).

invariant-parity-check-branch-reachabili: Parity-audit rule for native procs: a Python SimProcedure's kwarg/flag names an INTENT, not a branch that runs. Before filing a Rust-vs-Python divergence, check the flag's branch is reachable for the inputs the native proc actually accepts. Canonical miss (angr-j0dp3): fdopen.py passes create_file=True for w/w+/a/a+, but SimSystemPosix::_get_concrete_fd only materializes its /tmp/angr_implicit_N file on the solver.eval_one -> SimSolverError branch, i.e. a MULTI-SOLUTION SYMBOLIC fd. Concrete fds are returned unchanged whatever the mode, and native procs declared with 'concrete' args never see a symbolic one -- so a whole class of posix-plugin 'symbolic fallback' code (get_concrete_fd, get_fd concretization, close()'s eval_one) is dead for native and cannot be a divergence source. Same shape applies to any Python-side eval_one/concretize-on-demand path.
invariant-parse-type-width-not-none: vex/opcode_map.rs `parse_type` returning None is NOT a safe 'refuse to guess' signal: every caller in vex/pyvex_bridge.rs (Get/Load/CCall-retty/RegArray-elemTy/tyenv sites) and vex/libvex_lifter.rs::c_type_parse goes through opcode_map.rs::parse_type_or_log, which defaults to IRType::I64. So an unmapped Ity_* becomes 64 bits (loudly since angr-c7xno.90 — parse_type_or_log log::warn!s and carries the SILENT(cat-c) tag — but still wrongly). When a VEX type has no IRType variant, map it to the SAME-WIDTH variant rather than dropping to None. IRType is a width tag only -- nothing outside IRType::bits()/bytes() matches on which variant it is, and IRType::F80 is not constructible from any path except this table. Fixed at iter165: Ity_D32->I32, Ity_D64->I64, Ity_F128/Ity_D128->V128 (previously F80 = 80 bits for a 128-bit type). Latent-only; PPC/S390X are the sole emitters and are unsupported arches.
invariant-partial-cache-coverage-must-ov: invariant: a *partial* hit in a memory-layer cache must never let the layer below answer for the bytes the cache already owns. The Rust interpreter's callback-path load ladder (interpreter/expressions_loads.rs::load_concrete_addr) shipped this bug twice: PendingStoreBuffer::try_load needs one store covering the whole load, try_load_assembled needs every byte buffered (angr-6cp06.69), and both refuse partial coverage — so a store-1-byte-then-load-2 fell through to the flushed-store / concrete-cache / Python-callback rungs, which answered for BOTH bytes and silently undid the buffered write (angr-6cp06.88). Correct shape: resolve the lower rungs FIRST (load_concrete_addr_below_pending), then splice the covered bytes over that result via bv_utils::splice_bytes_over_bv. The splice must NOT go through bv_to_bytes for a non-Concrete base: bv_to_bytes zeroes a symbolic value and drops a Constrained's constraints, so every non-Concrete variant is rebuilt as a Concat of per-byte lanes with Extract for the uncovered ones. Applies to any new rung added to this ladder, and to memory/ sidecar lookups with the same all-or-nothing shape. Still unhandled by design: a pending *symbolic* store partially covering a load (symbolic_store_load is full-coverage-only), and get_return_addr's probe in interpreter/simprocedures.rs, which deliberately does not mirror the overlay rung.
invariant-pointer-keyed-dedup-must-pin: Pointer-keyed identity in the Rust engine (address-as-key dedup) is only sound while every keyed value is SIMULTANEOUSLY ALIVE — a freed node's address is immediately reusable, so a later distinct node reads as an already-seen hit and inherits the dead one's id. Any address-keyed map must therefore PIN what it keys. Two instances: claripy_bridge/cache.rs's EXPRESSION_BY_OPERANDS_PTR pins the operands Arc for imports (documented in claripy_bridge/mod.rs's header); symbolic/sharing.rs's ConstraintSharingWalk did NOT, and since SymContext::fold_sharing_walk keys the Vec that get_assumed_constraints() clones and drops per state, consecutive states landed on the same freed addresses and analyze_constraint_sharing collapsed unique_pointers/unique_shapes toward 1 (angr-gkcxh). Fix shape: make the entry point take the batch BY VALUE and retain it until the accumulator is consumed, and make the by-borrow entry point private so the footgun is unreachable. Retention must be a Vec<Vec<T>>, never one flat Vec — a flat Vec reallocates as batches accumulate and moves already-keyed nodes out from under their recorded addresses (growing the outer Vec only moves inner Vec headers; element buffers stay put).
invariant-proc-address-arith-wrapping:
Address arithmetic in native/angr/src/procedures/ AND native/angr/src/syscalls/ must use wrapping_* -- [profile.release] sets no overflow-checks, so a plain `src + size` panics under CI's release-checked profile and SILENTLY WRAPS in release (the shipped .so), turning a range test into a wrong answer rather than a crash. Concrete case fixed 2026-08-02 (angr-9ke6b.110): NativeMemmove's overlap check was `dst > src && dst < src + size`, the one non-wrapping site in memcpy.rs; near u64::MAX it misclassified an overlapping move as non-overlapping and copied forward, clobbering unread source bytes. Wrap-safe spelling of 'dst is strictly inside [src, src+size)' is `let d = dst.wrapping_sub(src); d != 0 && d < size` -- see fn memmove_copies_backward. Grep new procs/syscalls for bare + / - on address or address+length operands; syscalls/ was swept 2026-08-11 (angr-03vl4.65/.66/.67: store_stat_u64/u32/zero96 in file_path/stat_layouts.rs, getrlimit in rlimit.rs, gettimeofday/clock_gettime in sim_time.rs).

TEST RECIPE for a non-vacuous near-u64::MAX regression test (the trap: pass a huge pointer and the FIRST memory_store errors Unmapped and `?`-returns before the wrapping expression is ever evaluated, so the test passes with or without the fix). Do all three: (1) map BOTH the top page (0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_F000, 0x1000) and page 0, so the pre-wrap and post-wrap addresses are storable; (2) pick the base so every field store stays aligned within one page and none straddles the u64 boundary -- u64::MAX-7 works for 8-byte-aligned layouts (field 0 lands in the top page, every later offset wraps into page 0); (3) PROVE non-vacuity by temporarily restoring the bare + and confirming the test panics under `cargo test --profile release-checked`. Examples: gettimeofday_tv_near_u64_max_wraps_second_field (sim_time_tests.rs), fstat_statbuf_near_u64_max_wraps_field_offsets (file_path_fstat_tests.rs).
invariant-proxy-gate-callback-only-store: flareon2015_5 gate-on root cause (angr-5rjbq): under the callback-memory-proxy gate, the memory_store / memory_store_symbolic_value Python callbacks are DELIBERATE NO-OPS (state.memory *is* Rust memory; re-entering run() through the proxy double-borrows). The VEX interpreter's handle_symbolic_store Single branch and handle_concrete_store's use_sym_store branch dispatched stores ONLY to those callbacks, so under the gate the value was dropped outright and read back as structurally concrete <BV8 0>. Gate-off worked only because Python's real memory absorbed it. INVARIANT: any store the interpreter routes exclusively through a Python memory callback must also land in rust_memory when the proxy gate is on. angr-5mnx3.23 found four MORE sites that had repeated the raw dispatch (handle_storeg's two symbolic-guard branches, cas_store_symbolic_data, build_ite_store_from_callbacks) -- the pairing was a convention, not a structure. Enforcement now: VEXInterpreter::store_symbolic_value_buffered (interpreter/statements_store.rs) bundles buffer_store_for_rust_memory + call_memory_store_symbolic_value, and is the ONLY sanctioned way to reach that callback. A new store path calls it, never the callback directly. Callers needing the pending buffer drained first flush BEFORE the helper.
invariant-pymethods-caller-census-crosse: A #[pymethods] fn's caller census cannot be established from the Rust side: its real callers live in angr/exploration/*.py and are invisible to a native/ grep and to the compiler (nothing goes dead when the last Rust caller disappears). Two failure modes seen: (a) a doc comment asserting 'today the only caller passes X' (drop_state_from_stash claimed '_copies' while rust_manager.py::_route_preinit_seed_finds passed "active" and rust_state_proxy.py::_StashDict.__setitem__ passed any key), which then labels a live branch as dead defensive code a maintainer may delete -- here that would have reintroduced the angr-myzjx.25 SelectionPolicy memo leak; (b) the mirror-image gap where only the Rust-exercised argument value has a test. RULE for any comment or audit on a #[pymethods] surface: grep angr/**/*.py for the method name before writing a caller/argument claim, and prefer stating the invariant the branch upholds over enumerating who calls it today. Same spirit as CLAUDE.md's no-cardinality rule, one language boundary further out. Found angr-6cp06.16, commit 91df6296b.
invariant-pymethods-macro-expansion: PyO3 gotcha for DRY passes over #[pymethods]: a macro_rules! invocation placed INSIDE a '#[pymethods] impl T { ... }' block is invisible to pyo3 — the proc-macro attribute parses the impl before declarative macros expand, so it sees an ImplItem::Macro and the generated fns are never registered on the Python type (they silently just don't exist at runtime; it does not fail to compile). To collapse repeated pymethods bodies, have the macro emit its OWN '#[pymethods] impl T { ... }' block at module level and invoke it after the main block — this works because Cargo.toml enables the 'multiple-pymethods' feature. Canonical example: postcard_pickle_methods! in native/angr/src/fuzzer/corpus.rs (angr-12jjk.27).
invariant-pyo3-count-before-with-capacit: Any Vec::with_capacity / reserve whose count crosses the PyO3 boundary must be bounded BEFORE the reservation. This crate is panic=abort, so both failure modes are uncatchable process aborts, not Rust errors a caller can handle: 'capacity overflow' panics when count*size_of::<T>() exceeds isize, and alloc::handle_alloc_error aborts for a huge-but-not-overflowing count. No guest input is needed — an ordinary documented Python call (RustExplorationManager::register_simprocedure with a bogus num_args) is enough. Two fix shapes, pick by whether the refusal should degrade or raise. (a) Degrade: a named MAX_* const next to the error enum + a new error variant returned before the reservation, so the caller falls back (native dispatcher -> Python SimProcedure) instead of crashing — arch::MAX_EXTRACT_ARGS / ExtractionError::TooManyArgs guarding exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi (angr-0jh0j.23). (b) Raise at the trust boundary: a MAX_* const + a check_*(op, n) -> Result<(), String> guard called by every Python-facing entry point, message-typed rather than error-typed so the layer defining it stays pyo3-free and callers reporting through different channels (PyValueError vs BridgeError) can share it — symbolic::width_guards::check_bv_width is the precedent, symbolic::bv_chunk::check_concrete_load_size / MAX_CONCRETE_LOAD_BYTES the second instance (angr-0jh0j.11). Shape (b) is what a *generic* helper wants when it cannot construct its own error type E: guard at the boundaries, and additionally cap the helper's own reservation (Vec::with_capacity(n.min(MAX)) — bounds the allocation without truncating the result, since the loop still grows the vec as data arrives) as defence in depth for future callers. A bound like this also retroactively makes downstream index arithmetic (i * ptr_size) provably non-overflowing.
invariant-pyo3-getters-mask-dead-fields: A `#[pyo3(get)]` getter suppresses rustc's dead_code lint for the field it wraps — the derive counts as a read. So a pyclass whose Python surface is unreachable can hide arbitrarily much dead Rust state behind it, invisibly, forever. Removing DeferredFork's unreachable PyO3 surface (angr-03vl4.6) immediately exposed `push_level`, a third always-zero copy of the counter already killed twice in SymContext (angr-ph300.44, angr-c7xno.75); nothing had ever read it from Rust. Rule: when auditing a #[pyclass] for reachability, delete the getters FIRST and re-run clippy before concluding the change is cosmetic — the field-level cascade is where the real finding usually is. Same shape applies to #[pyo3(set)] and #[pymethods] accessors generally.
invariant-pyo3-multiple-pymethods-enable: PyO3 'multiple-pymethods' IS now enabled in this project (native/angr/Cargo.toml pyo3 features = [py-clone, abi3-py310, multiple-pymethods], angr-9ke6b.50). A pyclass may have MANY #[pymethods] impl blocks, in any module in the crate. RustExplorationManager's ~228-method surface is split across manager_methods.rs (construction/config/callbacks) + manager_methods_{hooks,state,constraints,procedures,techniques,export,run,stats}.rs, one #[pymethods] block each, all opened with 'use super::*;'. The old (A)/(B) workarounds in pyo3-pymethods-child-module-split are no longer forced -- you may now peel a cohesive method group into its own file+block directly. Two costs the flip carries, both handled: (1) it pulls in the 'inventory' crate (linker-section class registration) and pyo3 documents a compile-time cost; (2) SURPRISE -- see invariant-pyo3-multiple-pymethods-unmasks-unreachable-pub.
invariant-pyo3-multiple-pymethods-unmask: SURPRISE (angr-9ke6b.50): enabling pyo3's 'multiple-pymethods' feature UNMASKS 391 unreachable_pub warnings crate-wide, instantly reddening the CI clippy -D warnings gate (lib.rs has #![warn(unreachable_pub)] from angr-9ke6b.214). Verified empirically both ways: 0 hits at HEAD without the feature, 391 with it, split across solver.rs(78), callbacks/mod.rs(56), segmentlist.rs(27), the manager_methods*.rs files, callbacks/config.rs, automaton/python_bindings.rs. Mechanism: pyo3's NON-multiple-pymethods codegen was masking the lint on every #[pymethods] method AND on the #[pyclass] struct those blocks belong to. So the lint never actually covered the pyo3 surface -- the flip does not create new over-broad pubs, it reveals pre-existing ones. FIX CHOSEN: a scoped #[allow(unreachable_pub, reason=...)] on each affected #[pymethods] impl block and #[pyclass] struct (16 files, ~25 attributes), which restores EXACTLY the pre-feature coverage. Rejected alternative: rewriting 391 'pub fn' -> 'pub(crate) fn' (mechanically safe -- unreachable_pub proves external targets cannot reach them -- but a ~400-line diff mixing two concerns, and it risks a second dead_code wave). Do NOT blanket-allow unreachable_pub at crate level; that kills the guardrail for real Rust API surface. Note the pyclass STRUCT needs its own allow separately from its #[pymethods] block.
invariant-pyo3-single-pymethods-impl: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-02 by invariant-pyo3-multiple-pymethods-enabled -- the feature IS now on (angr-9ke6b.50) and a pyclass may have MANY #[pymethods] blocks. Kept for the still-true sub-facts: (B) a #[pymethods] block does NOT have to live in the same file as its #[pyclass]; a sibling module opened with 'use super::*;' surfaces the parent's private 'use' imports, pub(crate) fields and type aliases so bodies compile unchanged (demonstrated by state/pymethods.rs holding the whole #[pymethods] impl PyRustSimState while the #[pyclass] struct + inner()/inner_mut() stay in state/mod.rs, 7ac9c0fe2). (A) the thin-wrapper-in-pymethods / pub(crate)-body-in-sibling-plain-impl pattern (exploration/run_loop.rs, pending_api.rs, stepping.rs, resume.rs, helpers.rs) is still the right split when the body is large -- it is now a style choice, not a constraint.
invariant-pyo3-unreachable-pub-allow: Convention for pyo3 items flagged by unreachable_pub (angr-9ke6b.50, lib.rs 'unreachable_pub' note): a #[pyclass] struct or #[pymethods] impl block that trips the lint gets a scoped #[allow(unreachable_pub, reason = "pyo3 ...")] with the VERBATIM reason string used in segmentlist.rs/solver.rs -- do NOT narrow it to pub(crate). Rationale: those items are reached from Python, not Rust, so their Rust visibility is decorative, and the allow restores exactly the coverage pyo3's pre-multiple-pymethods codegen used to mask. Narrowing works and clippy goes green either way, so the wrong fix is easy to land; check the existing allow sites before choosing. Non-pyo3 items keep the opposite rule (narrow to pub(crate), angr-9ke6b.214) so dead_code can see them.
invariant-python-predicate-use-is-truthy: When Rust evaluates a caller-supplied Python *predicate*'s return value, test it with Bound::is_truthy()? — never extract::<bool>(py).unwrap_or(false). Python filter/predicate functions conventionally return any truthy object (a non-empty list/str, a numpy bool, an object with __bool__), and strict bool extraction reads those as FALSE, i.e. 'doesn't match'. It also swallows an exception raised from __bool__ into the same silent 'no match'. Found live in _move_states (exploration/state_lifecycle.rs) at angr-sqfj8.31. DISTINCTION: extract::<bool>() is still correct where the code is *discriminating a type* rather than testing truth — e.g. claripy_bridge/export.rs's compare_dunder, which asks 'did __eq__ return a Python bool (concrete) or a claripy AST?' and must NOT coerce the AST branch to a bool. Rule of thumb: truth test -> is_truthy()?; 'is it a bool?' -> extract/downcast, and propagate rather than unwrap_or.
invariant-qdmull-vex-op: Iop_QDMull16Sx4/32Sx2 (signed doubling saturating widening multiply, NEON VQDMULL, (I64,I64)->V128) map to IROp::VQDMull{elem,count} in vex/opcode_map_vector.rs (parse_vector). Implemented by vec_qdmull in ops/vec_permute_mul.rs: same full-lane widening layout as vec_mull (even=false, always signed), plus *2 and signed saturation to 2N bits. Saturation only fires on MIN*MIN (both -2^(N-1)): doubled product 2^(2N-1) clamps to 2^(2N-1)-1. Symbolic path widens inputs to out_width+2 bits before doubling to avoid overflow, then reuses saturate_lane_symbolic (widened to pub(super) in ops/vec_saturate.rs). Only 16Sx4/32Sx2 exist in libVEX; the QDMulHi/QRDMulHi high-half family is still unmapped.
invariant-rangemap-inverted-range-aborts: panic=abort makes any Python-supplied size a PROCESS-ABORT vector, not a catchable error. native/angr/Cargo.toml sets [profile.release] panic="abort", so nothing below is recoverable at the PyO3 boundary. Two shapes seen so far: (1) rangemap::RangeMap::{insert,remove} assert!(range.start < range.end), so an 'address..address + size' built from Python values without a checked_add guard aborts -- fixed in SegmentList::release (native/angr/src/segmentlist.rs, angr-9ke6b.199); SegmentList::occupy already had it. Convention: 'let Some(end) = address.checked_add(size) else { return; }' tagged // SILENT(cat-a), since a wrapping range describes no real region. (2) allocating a buffer whose length came straight from Python -- Vec's 'capacity overflow' panic near usize::MAX and handle_alloc_error for a merely huge size both abort. Fixed in Icicle::mem_read (native/angr/src/icicle.rs) via the free fn checked_read_len: reject a wrapping addr+size and a size above Icicle::max_mem_read_bytes (the mmu's own capacity()*page_size()), THEN allocate. Rule for new code: validate the range/length before you build it, whether the consumer is a RangeMap or the allocator; a free fn taking (addr, size, max) keeps it unit-testable where the surrounding type needs a VM/GIL.
invariant-recognizer-parser-grammar-pari:
Recognizer/value-parser grammar parity is an invariant for any native proc that returns BOTH a value and a consumed-length (strtod/strtol/strtoul/sscanf-family). If the boundary-finder accepts a grammar the value-parser cannot handle, the result is the worst failure shape: a wrong value reported with *endptr advanced past the whole literal, so the caller believes a full correct parse happened. Concrete instance (angr-sqfj8.81, commit 98cc4c8fc): procedures/strtod.rs floating_prefix_len recognized C99 hex-floats but the value went through f64::from_str, which REJECTS hex-float syntax outright ('0x1.8p3'.parse::<f64>() is Err) -- .unwrap_or(0.0) made strtod("0x1.8p3") return 0.0 instead of 12.0. Rust std has NO hex-float parser; strtod.rs::parse_hex_float is the crate's only one (u128 significand + sticky bit past 124 bits for round-to-nearest-even, plus scale_by_pow2 = musl's three-step scalbn clamp so the exponent tails don't collapse through an intermediate inf/0). Reuse those two, do not hand-roll a second. Review rule: when auditing a proc with a prefix-scanner, diff the scanner's documented grammar against what the value parser actually accepts -- and prefer deferring to Python (ProcedureError::NotImplemented) over substituting a default on a prefix the value parser rejects.

BACKTRACK COROLLARY (angr-6cp06.2, commit 19528862f). The same scanners have a second failure mode on the OTHER side: when a longer alternative fails mid-scan, C's longest-valid-subject-sequence rule requires backtracking to the longest valid SHORTER prefix, not rejecting to the start. The natural Rust spelling -- capture 'prefix_start' at the top, 'return prefix_start' from every failure path -- is wrong wherever a shorter alternative already matched, and it silently drops the sign too because prefix_start is captured before the sign is consumed. floating_prefix_len's hex branch did exactly this: '0x' with no hex digit after it returned prefix_start, so strtod("0xg") reported end_offset 0 and strtod("-0xz") returned +0.0 at offset 0, where glibc gives 0.0/offset 1 and -0.0/offset 2 (the leading '0' is itself a complete decimal literal). Fix is to return the index of the byte that broke the longer alternative. Review rule: for each 'return <start>' in a prefix scanner, ask whether a shorter alternative had already succeeded at that point -- and check the sign is inside, not outside, the returned span. The strtol sibling (bd angr-bmfj0, commit afe68fd7e) shows the PREFERRED FIX SHAPE: rather than patching what the failure path returns, add a lookahead guard so the scanner never consumes the longer alternative it cannot complete -- strtol.rs::hex_prefix_has_digit gates both 0x-consuming sites in parse_concrete_prefix, leaving the '0' for the digit parser, which then reports value and endptr through the normal SUCCESS path (consumed > 0). That matters because the failure path in these procs is usually governed by a separate, often-divergent 'no conversion' rule (run_strtol points *endptr past the prefix, not at nptr as C says); routing a genuine conversion through it makes the fix depend on a quirk that a later correctness pass would break. Corollary for symbolic engines: a symbolic lookahead byte must count as USABLE (consume the prefix, let the accumulator decide), else constrained-to-digits buffers regress.
invariant-refusal-guard-infallible-fallb: Refusal-guard placement invariant (angr-0jh0j.35): when you fix an overflow/validation bug by making a fallible entry point REFUSE the bad input, check what the new Err path reaches. A refusal can route the bad value straight INTO an infallible fallback that swallows errors and then performs the same unguarded arithmetic — in memory/, check_access_size in SymbolicMemory::load_concrete_common makes an oversize load fail, and SymbolicMemory::load_concrete_or_unconstrained's by-design 'every error becomes an unconstrained value' branch then computed the very size*8 the guard existed to prevent. Two consequences: (1) an infallible fabricator needs its own clamped-width helper (memory::fabricate_width_bits) so the unreachable case degrades to a wrong-but-valid value rather than an invalid one (a 0-width BV Z3 cannot represent); (2) guards must ALSO sit on entry points that short-circuit before the shared body — load_symbolic/load_symbolic_unified reach unconstrained_read_value under AVOID_MULTIVALUED_READS without touching a page. Generalizes to any error-swallowing fallback (native-proc ProcedureError bounce, ITE-leaf fillers), not just memory. THIRD consequence (angr-0jh0j.84, found by audit one round later): fixing the sites a failing trace led you to is not the sweep — grep the whole file for the arithmetic SHAPE. .35 hardened two fabricate sites and left load_symbolic_unified's all-unmapped mem_all_unmapped_* arm on a bare size*8 for a full round, because no trace reached it (check_access_size refuses first, so it is unreachable defense-in-depth, not a live bug). When a helper like fabricate_width_bits is introduced, its doc should ENUMERATE its call sites — that list is what makes a missed site visible on the next read.
invariant-register-file-concrete-buffer: RegisterFile::copy_to_bytes (native/angr/src/arch/register_file.rs) zeroes the byte span of every entry in self.symbolic after copying self.data, because RegisterFile::put's symbolic branches never clear the concrete buffer: a register written concretely then overwritten symbolically leaves stale concrete bytes in data. INVARIANT for future edits: the flat register buffer is a CONCRETE-ONLY view — a byte that belongs to a symbolic register reads 0, and the symbolic value travels separately via ExplorationStateSnapshot::get_symbolic_register_names. Corollary for the wider audit family: self.data and self.symbolic are NOT kept mutually exclusive (put's sub-register compose branches deliberately write both), so any new reader of self.data must consult self.symbolic itself — RegisterFile::get and get_offset_u64 do; get_sp_value deliberately does not (documented fast concrete path). Also audited: get_registers_raw has NO Python caller — rust_state_export.py rebuilds registers from get_registers_named + get_symbolic_register_names.
invariant-register-file-le-storage-be-of: Rust RegisterFile storage is little-endian on EVERY arch, unconditionally. Big-endian register semantics (angr stores its register file at arch.register_endness — Iend_BE for MIPS32/MIPS64/ARMEB) are implemented by mirroring the *offset* in RegisterFile::mirror_offset (native/angr/src/arch/register_file.rs), never by changing the byte<->value composition. Consequences future work must respect: (1) do NOT make le_bytes_to_u128 / u128_le_byte / compose_range / put's overlay bit arithmetic / RegisterFile::merge's concrete-diff chunk scan / get_sp_value endianness-aware — that would double-apply on top of the mirror; (2) endianness is a CALLER-supplied fact, never derivable from the arch: RegisterFile::new_with_endian(arch, is_le) and VEXInterpreter::with_config_endian(arch, ctx, config, is_le) are the two production constructors, and RegisterFile::new / VEXInterpreter::new are #[cfg(test)] LE-only conveniences precisely so a new production caller cannot silently pick LE (angr-21cz6). A new big-endian arch must also list every register in its CANONICAL table, since mirror_offset is the identity for an offset no canonical entry covers; (3) the mirror is an involution and the identity for a whole-register access, so name-keyed get_reg/put_reg and the Python<->Rust value-level sync are unaffected; (4) Arch::is_little_endian() is hardcoded true on every arch — the real answer is the state's little_endian override, seeded in rust_manager.py from project.arch.memory_endness (verified equal to register_endness on every archinfo arch as of 2026-08-16); the exploration path never has to re-derive it because exploration/step_core.rs does 'interp.registers = state.registers().fork()'; (5) TWO COORDINATE SPACES, never mix them (angr-6cp06.74): RegisterFile::get/put take a RAW VEX offset and mirror on entry, but every key of self.symbolic and every index into self.data is already a STORAGE offset. Code that iterates those keys and then wants to read must call RegisterFile::get_storage (the un-mirroring body of get), NOT get — RegisterFile::merge did the latter for its four read sites and double-mirrored, landing on the other half of the containing register. The involution property does NOT rescue a double application here, because the doubly-mirrored value is used as a real lookup key and bit-range reference against actual storage entries, not merely recomputed. Invisible on every LE arch and on every merge test that uses the LE-only RegisterFile::new — a BE regression test is mandatory for any new merge/overlay-scanning code (see arch/register_file_tests.rs::be_merge_reads_the_other_side_in_storage_coordinates). angr-fuhmm, angr-21cz6, angr-6cp06.74.
invariant-register-merge-width-mismatch: RegisterFile::merge (native/angr/src/arch/register_file.rs) width-mismatch merge, angr-9ke6b.13: when two forked paths hold symbolic values of DIFFERENT widths at the same register offset (path A wrote eax/32-bit, path B wrote rax/64-bit at the same VEX offset), the merge used to keep self's value and drop other's — an unsound merge. Fix: widen BOTH sides to max(width) by calling RegisterFile::get(offset, size, ctx) on each file (get composes that file's own symbolic overlay with its own concrete backing bytes, so this is DRY — no hand-rolled zero-extend), then ITE at the common width, and drop overlays strictly INSIDE the widened span the same way put does. TRAP that forced a restructure: the merge loop iterates a HashSet<u32> of offsets, so mutating self.symbolic mid-loop while the widening arm READS self via get() would make the result depend on iteration order — merged values are now staged into a Vec and applied after the loop. Tests: merge_width_mismatch_ite_merges_both_paths (mock ctx, walks the expr tree via RustBV::operands() — Debug on RustBV prints 'Expression(Ite, 64, 3 operands)' and does NOT render operand symbol names, so a format!("{:?}") substring check silently fails) and merge_width_mismatch_selects_each_path_under_solver (real SymContext + push/add_constraint/is_sat/pop).
invariant-register-names-subset-of-canon: REGISTER-TABLE PLACEMENT RULE (angr-9ke6b.9): any name listed in a per-arch REGISTER_NAMES export slice MUST also live in that arch's CANONICAL table, never ALIASES-only. register_name(offset) scans CANONICAL only, so an exported-but-aliased name resolves forward (name->offset) but not backward (offset->name). X86 shipped exactly that for xmm0..7 + the x87/SSE control words, making X86::register_name(XMM0) return None while AMD64::register_name resolved it. Fixed by moving the SSE/x87 block into x86.rs CANONICAL; forward lookups are unchanged because lookup_register_offset/size check CANONICAL then ALIASES. Gate: arch/registry_tests.rs::exported_register_names_reverse_resolve asserts, for every arch in ALL_ARCHES and every name in register_names(), that register_name(register_offset(name)) is Some and round-trips to the same offset (it compares offsets, not name identity, so 'pc' vs 'eip' canonicalization at a shared offset is allowed). Complements the opposite-direction rule in invariant-guest-state-size-vs-archinfo: the VEX bookkeeping fields (emnote/cmstart/cmlen/nraddr/ip_at_syscall) stay ALIASES-only precisely because they are NOT exported via REGISTER_NAMES.
invariant-register-names-u128-width: INVARIANT: Arch::register_names() (the per-arch REGISTER_NAMES const in arch/amd64.rs, x86.rs, arm.rs, ...) is the set of registers that cross the Python boundary — it drives register_names_for_arch (Python _supported_register_names in rust_state_sync.py) and RustSimState::export_full's named_registers. It is EXACTLY that arch's CANONICAL table minus entries wider than 16 bytes, in BOTH directions: ExplorationStateSnapshot::get_registers_named carries each value as a u128 and RegisterFile::get's concrete read composes bytes with 'value |= (byte as u128) << (i*8)', so a wider register silently yields garbage (release-mode shift masking) instead of failing; and a narrow CANONICAL entry left OUT of REGISTER_NAMES is silently filtered by _supported_register_names, so set_registers_bulk drops every state.regs.<name> write for that arch while the same write works on a sibling arch. Today x86/AMD64 'fpreg' (64 B, 8 x87 slots) is the only legitimate omission. Both directions are now machine-gated in arch/registry_tests.rs: register_names_all_resolve_and_fit_in_u128 (forward) and every_narrow_canonical_register_is_exported (converse, angr-sqfj8.6) — the latter reads the whole table via Arch::canonical_registers(), a test-only assertion primitive generated for all six arches by impl_arch_registers!. Width is the converse test's ONLY exemption, deliberately: no per-arch allowlist that can drift. History of this bug class: angr-9ke6b.6 added fptag/fpround/fc3210/ftop and left a HARDCODED field-list test (x87_control_registers_round_trip_through_register_names), which by construction only covers registers someone already thought of — it missed X86 sseround, fixed a sweep later in angr-sqfj8.1 (commit 6626d4df6). When adding a register to any CANONICAL table, add it to REGISTER_NAMES too unless it is >16 B.
invariant-register-overlay-keys-are-unal: RegisterFile.symbolic (native/angr/src/arch/mod.rs) is keyed by RAW VEX guest-state offset, and those keys are NOT register-aligned: x86/amd64 register the high-byte aliases ah/ch/dh/bh at GPR_offset+1 (see ALIASES in arch/amd64.rs and arch/x86.rs). Any code that scans the overlay map in arch-word-sized chunks and tests only the chunk's aligned start offset will miss an overlay living inside the chunk. That exact assumption produced angr-c7xno.1 (RegisterFile::merge's concrete-diff loop compared raw backing bytes for such a chunk and inserted a concrete-only ITE at the aligned offset, which get() then returned verbatim on a width match — silently shadowing the already-merged ah). The safe shapes: test the whole range [off, off+reg_bytes) for membership, and when an inner overlay exists compose both sides through RegisterFile::get (which walks the map for covering/contained overlays) rather than reading self.data directly. Whenever you insert a wide overlay that covers narrower ones, also drop the inner keys (the 'widened' subsumption pass in merge) — leaving both is hazardous because put() composes a sub-register write into the WIDER entry it finds and leaves the narrow duplicate stale, after which get()'s exact-offset hit returns the stale one.
invariant-registerfile-arc-cow-makemut: RegisterFile (native/angr/src/arch/mod.rs) stores registers as data: Arc<Vec<u8>> (NOT Vec<u8>) since angr-6t8z3.1. fork()/derived Clone share the buffer O(1) via Arc::clone; the deep copy happens lazily on first write. EVERY &mut self register write MUST route through Arc::make_mut(&mut self.data) or it will silently leak across the fork boundary (CoW broken). Current write sites: put()'s three concrete-write loops + copy_from_bytes(). set_ip/set_sp delegate to put; merge mutates only self.symbolic. Reads index self.data[..] directly (Deref). Serde shadow RegisterFileData.data stays Vec<u8>: From<RegisterFile> uses Arc::unwrap_or_clone, From<RegisterFileData> wraps Arc::new. Faithfulness gate: test_register_file_fork_cow_isolation in arch/register_file_tests.rs. Measured state_fork bench -9.6%. Extends invariant-symbolic-memory-fork-fields CoW discipline to registers.
invariant-regression-guard-citations-unv: A 'Regression guard: <test name>' citation in a Rust doc comment is unverified prose — nothing compiles or resolves it, so a fabricated or renamed name reads exactly like a real one and the invariant it claims coverage for may in fact have NONE. context.rs's three-gate SharedLineageSolver doc cited two test names (test_lineage_minted_only_when_opted_in / test_lineage_not_minted_under_bare_push) that never existed anywhere in the repo (angr-5mnx3.44). When repairing such a citation, do not just rename it to the nearest real test: first check per-clause whether a guard exists for EACH claim the sentence covers. Two of the three gates had guards under other names in another file; gate (c) (invariant-v5ht-dismantle-child-none) had none, and the doc had been asserting otherwise for months. Second, related trap: a negative-assertion guard whose setup makes the asserted value ALSO the default proves nothing. Both existing gate guards asserted child.lineage_arc().is_none() from a parent whose own lineage was already None, so they could not distinguish 'refused to mint' from 'cloned a None' — the new gate-(c) test has to stage a parent that actually HOLDS a lineage. Mutation-verify any guard you add (neuter the arm, confirm the test reddens); an assertion that passes against the broken code is the same defect one layer down.
invariant-relative-growth-cap-is-not-abs: A host-safety bound expressed *relative* to a current value (e.g. syscalls/brk.rs's MAX_BRK_GROWTH capping new_brk - current, or any 'growth cap') does NOT bound the absolute value: repeated in-bounds steps walk the quantity to the top of the address space. Any align-up (x + PAGE_MASK & !PAGE_MASK) or +len downstream of such a bound must therefore be treated as reachable at u64::MAX, not dismissed as 'the cap prevents it'. Two failure modes seen in brk (angr-fs8kb.51): (1) an aligned-up *exclusive end* wraps to 0, so a 'while addr < end' page walk runs ZERO iterations -- the bug is a silently skipped safety check, not a hang or a crash, which is why it survived review and the overflow audit gate; (2) the byte-stepped 'addr += PAGE_SIZE' wraps past the final page. Fix shape: iterate PageIndex::range_covering(start, len) over page *numbers* and derive len from the LAST BYTE (new_end - 1) rather than an aligned-up exclusive end. See also invariant-proc-address-arith-wrapping.
invariant-reset-paths-clear-derived-fiel: INVARIANT (restore/reset paths must clear EVERY derived field, not just the primary container): four separate bugs of this exact shape landed in round 8's queue back-to-back -- RustExplorationManager::load_snapshot kept the pre-restore Python id-keyed shadow maps, load_snapshot_bytes kept the pre-restore ConstraintTracker sets, _reset_for_stage left the stage-1 uniqueness hashes live, and SegmentList::__setstate__ (segmentlist.rs) cleared self.map but not self.bytes_occupied. The shape: a struct keeps a primary container PLUS one or more incrementally-maintained derived fields (byte totals, id-keyed shadow maps, dedup hash sets, tracker sets) whose only mutator is a monotonic add. A restore/reset/load method clears the container, replays the saved entries through the normal add path, and the derived field silently reports old-value + restored-value. Two rules: (1) when adding a derived/cached field to a struct, grep that struct's impl for every clear/reset/load/__setstate__ method and extend each one; (2) when reviewing such a method, enumerate the struct's fields and check each is either reset or provably rebuilt by the replay -- a partial reset compiles and passes every fresh-instance test, because the in-tree caller is usually a pickle/new path that starts from Default. Reachability matters: a #[pymethods] fn is callable from arbitrary Python on a populated instance even when the in-tree protocol only ever hits it on a fresh one.
invariant-residual-sink-vs-assumed-ir: Constraints imported from Python via the Z3-ptr fast path (exploration::constraints::import_python_constraints, the shared body behind BOTH _add_constraints_to_state and _add_constraints_to_pending since angr-9ke6b.71) used to be recorded TWICE: add_constraint_raw logged them in the residual sink (SymContext::local_constraints.non_bv_assertions) AND the call site pushed an assumed IR pair. Invariant: the residual sink is ONLY for constraints with no RustBV form. Anything reconstructible from the assumed IR must go in via add_constraint_raw_assumed (constraint_ops.rs), which skips the residual push. Violating this silently breaks SymContext::unsat_core_assumed, which asserts residuals UNGUARDED (they have no claripy AST to blame) — a double-listed constraint is then pinned outside its assumption literal and the unsat core comes back EMPTY. Symptom looked context-dependent (only after a real RustExplorationManager swapped the Rust thread-local Z3 ctx for claripy's) because AST-identity dedup happens to catch the dup in a Rust-owned context but not in claripy's. The dual failure is just as bad and hit twice (angr-sqfj8.121, angr-03vl4.74): recording in NEITHER log. Every reconstruction path — to_snapshot's dump_non_bv_smtlib2, unsat_core_assumed, _export_state_constraints — rebuilds from the assumed + residual logs and NEVER from local_constraints.z3_assertions, so a constraint that is only in z3_assertions is enforced in-process and then vanishes on snapshot/restore. So: any new route that asserts on the live solver owes an EXACTLY-ONE-log push. If it asserts via add_constraint_raw* that is automatic; if it asserts by some other route (add_constraint_tracked_indexed must use assert_and_track for unsat-core fidelity) it must call assumed_constraints_push or SymContext::push_residual_assertion itself, branching on whether claripy_to_rustbv succeeded. See [[unsat-core-on-demand-not-tracked]]. UPDATE (angr-6cp06.26): the per-constraint body moved down one level into exploration::constraints::import_one_constraint — the single seam now shared by import_python_constraints (initial/pending, ConstraintTier::Z3PtrFirst) AND RustExplorationManager::sync_constraints_from_python (callback-bounce sync, ConstraintTier::RustBvFirst), which used to be an independent reimplementation with inverted tier precedence. Any new tier or exactly-one-log fix belongs in import_one_constraint, not in either wrapper.
invariant-result-type-width-from-opcode-: IROp::result_type() (vex/ir/ops_def.rs) must derive packed-vector widths from elem*count via the Self::width_total_to_type helper, never hardcode IRType::V128. The hardcoded arms were wrong in BOTH directions, not just the AVX2 one the audit bead flagged: opcode_map maps VAdd/VSub/VMul/VShlN/VShrN/VSarN/VCmpEQ/VCmpGT at D-reg NEON 64-bit totals (Iop_Add8x8 -> I64) as well as Q-reg/SSE 128 and AVX2 256 (Iop_Add8x32/16x16/32x8/64x4). Whenever an arm of result_type hardcodes a width, cross-check the corresponding parse_opcode arm in vex/opcode_map.rs (integer/special families) or its opcode_map_float.rs / opcode_map_vector.rs siblings for the full set of mapped shapes -- the two files are independent sources of truth and drift silently, because result_type is only consulted on the Err() fallback path of interpreter/expressions.rs (sizing a fresh-symbolic value) plus IRExpr::result_type in vex/ir/ast.rs, so a wrong width produces no test failure. The regression test test_packed_lane_result_type_tracks_mapped_width in vex/ir_tests.rs pins this by driving expectations through parse_opcode; extend it rather than writing a fresh literal-IROp test. Widening arms need their own rule: VMull{even=false}/VQDMull double lane width (2*elem*count) while VMull{even=true} (Iop_MullEven*) halves the lane count as the width doubles (elem*count). STATUS (angr-sqfj8.115, iter50): the hardcoded-V128 class is now EXHAUSTED -- the last group (VMin/VMax/VAbs/VFAdd/VFSub/VFMul/VFDiv/VFSqrt/VFAbs/VFNeg/VFMin/VFMax) was moved onto width_total_to_type and pinned in that test. No hardcoded packed-width arm remains; if a new one appears, it is a regression. ADDENDUM (angr-9ke6b.169, iter161): the TAG matters too, not just the width. No consumer of result_type compares IRType tags for equality -- every caller goes through .bits() -- so an I128-vs-V128 mismatch is invisible to tests and must be caught by cross-referencing the libVEX header. DivMod{U,S}128to64 was tagged I128; libVEX types it ':: V128,I64 -> V128', and our own opcode_map already models the surrounding chain as vector-typed (Iop_64HLtoV128 -> Concat{ty: V128} builds the dividend, Iop_V128to64 / Iop_V128HIto64 split the result), so the retag to V128 is runtime-neutral and internally consistent. Pinned by test_divmod_128_to_64_result_is_vector_tagged in vex/ir_tests.rs. Rule of thumb: when an op's operands or consumers in opcode_map use V128, its result_type must not say I128.
invariant-resume-fork-base-must-precede-:
invariant-resume-fork-base-must-precede-guard (FIXED angr-khpsh, commit on rust-symex 2026-07-22; EXTENDED angr-z3obp 2026-09-08): the deferred-fork base must NEVER carry the branch guard or the taken-path constraints at the moment build_unexplored_fork runs — on the snapshot-less arm it does base.fork_false/fork_true(condition), so a pre-guarded base makes the unexplored sibling UNSAT by construction and it silently lands in STASH_PRUNED instead of being explored. The snapshot arm is immune (it rebuilds from a pre-branch clone), which is why every instance of this bug has been latent-until-snapshotless.

RESUME HALF (angr-khpsh): in exploration/resume.rs, ALL THREE resume entry points derive the fork base from a state carrying NEITHER the branch guard NOR the deferred forks' taken-path constraints. _resume_after_simprocedure and _resume_after_symbolic_branch build fork_base = pending.pre_callback_snapshot.unwrap_or_else(|| state.fork()) BEFORE calling apply_deferred_fork_constraints(&state, ..); _deadend_pending_callback never calls it up front and passes the parking state as MaterializeForkCtx::guard_sink (distinct from fork_base, hence structurally immune). invariant-retiring-a-python-callback: Retiring a dead PythonCallbacks entry is a FOUR-place edit, not two (angr-9ke6b.218 item 1, commit 2a6643a07). Deleting PythonCallbacks::call_<x> alone leaves the field alive because callbacks/mod.rs drives fields through the with_callback_fields! macro list — the field must be dropped from that list AND from the struct AND the Python registration in rust_manager.py::_setup_callbacks AND the matching gil_profile::CallbackSite variant (which requires bumping CallbackSite::COUNT and the all() array — COUNT is a hand-maintained const, so a stale one is a compile error in all(), which is the good failure mode). Deleting a CallbackSite variant is safe for the ZeroPy gate: run_zeropy_gate.py spells GIL_CLASSES out explicitly and the per-site gil_work_ns_callback_<name> keys are generated from CallbackSite::all(), so a removed always-zero site just stops emitting a key nobody reads. Check for a dispatch_tests.rs 'callback not set' table entry too — it names the method by hand. (It was a FIVE-place edit until angr-0jh0j.6 generated the set_<x> pymethod from the with_callback_fields! list too — that one now disappears with the list entry.)
invariant-reverse-z3-roundtrip-tests: Invariant for Reverse/Concat Z3 emission in native/angr/src/symbolic/value_z3.rs: any Reverse-related code change MUST include a Z3 round-trip test that pins the inner BV to a concrete value and asserts ctx.eval returns the byte-reversed value. Cargo-only structural checks (e.g. 'parts assemble in this order') won't catch the bug class because Z3 silently folds mis-shaped concats back to x via its bv_rewriter. Pattern: test_reverse_z3_emission_{16,32,64}bit_leaf and test_reverse_z3_emission_concat_of_bytes added 2026-05-19 in value_simplify_tests.rs.
invariant-rust-as-cast-is-rne-only: Rust's `as` float cast (f64 as f32, float as int) is hard-wired to round-nearest-ties-to-even — it CANNOT express the VEX directed modes (rm&0x3: 1=-inf, 2=+inf, 3=zero). So in native/angr/src/vex/ops/conversions.rs any _rm-suffixed op whose concrete closure names its parameter `_rm` and reaches for a bare `as` cast is a silent-wrong-answer bug, not a style nit: it returns the RNE result under every mode with no error and no fallback (angr-c7xno.85 was exactly this for Iop_F64toF32; the open lint bead angr-91vj9.7 is meant to catch the class). Two correct patterns already in the file: float->INT uses ops::float_arith::apply_rounding (generic over IeeeNum since angr-6cp06.38; was Self::apply_rounding_f32/f64) -- round to an integer first, then cast; float->FLOAT narrowing uses VEXOps::narrow_f64_to_f32_rm — take the RNE result, and if widening it back is not bit-equal to the source, step ONE ULP toward the requested direction with next_up()/next_down(). That ULP step also buys IEEE-754 overflow saturation (+inf.next_down() == f32::MAX, so RZ/RD saturate instead of overflowing) and subnormal underflow (0.0.next_up() is the smallest subnormal, so RU on a tiny value does not flush to zero) with no special-casing. TRAP when testing: the RNE-implicit unop stub (VEXOps::unop(IROp::F64toF32, ..)) is NOT the path the interpreter takes — eval_binop routes the real 2-operand form into VEXOps::binop, so a test that only drives unop cannot see an rm bug at all.
invariant-rust-concrete-arith-must-wrap: Concrete integer arithmetic in the Rust VEX ops MUST use wrapping_*/checked_* helpers, never bare / % + << *. Rust checks division overflow even in --release, and the workspace [profile.release] sets panic="abort", so any overflow panic (classic: i128::MIN / -1 in a signed DivMod) SIGABRTs the whole Python process — no catchable PanicException, no errored stash, all exploration lost (no catch_unwind in the step path). Z3 bvsdiv/bvsrem wrap, so wrapping_div/wrapping_rem match the symbolic path exactly. Fixed in divmod_double_to_single (native/angr/src/vex/ops/int_arith.rs) for DivModS128to64, angr-n0xru. Audit-driven bugs of this shape should grep other concrete arithmetic arms for bare operators.
invariant-rustbv-rewrite-second-hook: RustBV IR rewrites can be bypassed: extract_into / truncate_into / extract_no_ctx all exist as ways to construct Extract nodes in value.rs. Only extract_into runs the canonicalization rules (Rule 1-5 at value.rs:1540-1605). truncate_into (used heavily by vex/ops.rs at 309, 356, 3023) and extract_no_ctx (used by arch/register_file.rs register slicing) build BVOp::Extract directly. Any IR rewrite that only fires inside extract_into therefore has a coverage gap. The fix from angr-p8cz: add a second hook point at Z3 emission (emit_extract_z3_cached in value.rs) that re-applies the rules. Pattern for future rewrite additions: hook at BOTH construction (extract_into) AND emission (emit_extract_z3_cached) to be self-correcting.
